subject: Post-call: SDK auth + JSON-output guarantees for Catalyst POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — SDK auth + JSON-output guarantees

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

What we heard (narrowed):
- You want a POC that demonstrates structured JSON outputs for invoice extraction and action routing, with at least 99% schema compliance on our evaluation suite.
- Main integration constraints: Catalyst runs behind an internal gateway, prefers short-lived credentials (OAuth or mTLS), and needs traffic routed regionally (US primary).
- You care about deterministic/validated outputs: constrained decoding where possible, and a validation + retry pattern for downstream systems.

Redwood proposal (high level):
1) SDK + auth: provide our SDK quickstart (API key + optional OAuth flow for short-lived tokens) and mTLS guidance for Private deployments.
2) Routing: request-level policy to route production traffic to a quantized low-latency model, fallback to higher-capacity model on failure.
3) Structured output reliability: combine constrained decoding (token/grammar constraints) for critical fields, plus a post-gen validator and deterministic retry loop (with adjusted sampling) for any failures.

Attachments: I dropped a short "redwood-sdk-integration-cheatsheet.pdf" and a proposed "catalyst-structured-output-requirements.docx" that summarize the patterns we discussed.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
- Dev sync: technical deep-dive with your engineering team (Tom) next Tue (4/14) — 60 min.
- POC kickoff: target week of 4/20. We’ll send a small SOW stub and a DocuSign link for approvals.
- Action: Tom to share a sample message schema + a small set of representative prompts (<= 50) we can use for baseline tests.

If that all looks right I’ll loop in the infra team and draft the SOW.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our side so Dev can scope the POC: 

1) When you say constrained decoding + validator + retry, can you outline the expected failure modes and SLA for retries? For instance, if the model fails schema validation how many retries do you attempt and do retries incur additional cost or latency guarantees?

2) Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens — OAuth sounds good. Is there a recommended rotation period you support for SDK-managed tokens? Also curious if mTLS is necessary only for Private deployments or whether it can be layered on top of hosted as an optional control.

3) Routing: we need assurance that traffic from our US gateway stays in-region and that fallback to another model doesn’t leak unredacted PII to an external region. Can Redwood support region-constrained fallbacks?

Finally, I can send over the sample schema (JSON Schema draft-07) and a few example prompts by EOD.

Regards,
Sara
Sara Lim
Head of AI Engineering, Catalyst AI

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call recap & next steps — SDK auth + JSON-output guarantees

Sara / Tom —

Thanks — good questions. I outlined a pragmatic pattern below that we use at Redwood for structured-output reliability; happy to walk through these in the dev sync. TL;DR: mix constrained decoding when feasible, prefer deterministic sampling (temp=0) for rigid fields, validate post-gen, and use a bounded re-prompt/retry strategy that escalates to a higher-capacity model when necessary.

Failure modes and retry SLAs:
- Validation failure (schema mismatch, missing required field, type error): perform up to 3 deterministic retries with increasingly strict decoding constraints (see code-like policy below). Each retry increments latency; we can keep overall P99 latency SLO at X ms for sync calls by moving longer retries to an async job or queued fallback. Retries are charged as normal tokens.
- Ambiguous content (model returns plausible but incorrect enum): run a reranker over N-best candidates (N=5) using an embeddings-based similarity score against your canonical examples; if confidence < threshold, flag for human review.

Decoding + validation pattern (pseudo-config):
- primary_generation: {model: "rwd-lowlat-v1", temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.7, max_tokens: 256, output_format: "json"}
- constrained_tokens: use a field-level whitelist/grammar for critical enums (invoice_date, currency_code, routing_action)
- validator: run JSON Schema (draft-07) + custom semantical checks (date ranges, currency codes)
- retry_policy: retries = 3; on_retry: reduce top_p by 0.15, enforce stricter token whitelist; after retry 3, escalate to high-cap model with expanded context (rwd-accurate-v2)

Auth & SDK:
- Hosted: API keys are supported for quickstarts; we recommend SDK-managed OAuth with refresh short-lived tokens (recommended rotation 1h–6h depending on your policy). Hosted with customer-managed VPC peering supports mTLS as an opt-in for additional assurance.
- Private: mTLS + KMS integration (HSM) is standard for on-prem or VPC installs.

Routing & region constraints:
- You can scope routing policies by origin IP / VPC tag to guarantee in-region serving. Fallback policies can be configured to only use models in the same region or in a customer-approved failover region — we'll enforce PII redaction rules on cross-region fallbacks if they are ever used.

Embeddings / reranker suggestions:
- For post-gen ranking, compute embedding of the generated candidates and compare against ground-truth embeddings (cosine similarity). Use a small in-memory store for the POC to keep latency low.

Small example: how a retry could look (plain text):
1) Gen1 @ temp=0.0, top_p=0.7 -> validate -> fail (missing total_amount)
2) Retry1 @ temp=0.0, top_p=0.55 + enforce numeric token-range grammar -> validate -> pass -> return
3) If still fail, escalate to rwd-accurate-v2 with extra context and set async fallback

We’ll include a short SDK snippet in the cheat-sheet showing how to flip sampling params and run the schema validator client-side.

If you can share the JSON schema and a handful of typical prompts, I’ll craft a baseline test harness and a short benchmark (schema pass rate, avg token cost, P99 latency).

—Dev
